title: Function Overloading Basics
learningObjectives: Describe function overloading and its purpose.
Compare overload candidates using parameter types/counts.
Trace overload selection for representative calls.
Recognize ambiguity and invalid return-type-only distinctions.
Create a coherent overload set and test each call.

understand.concept: Function overloading allows multiple functions with the same name when their parameter lists differ. Overload resolution uses the arguments and viable parameter types; return type alone cannot distinguish overloads.
understand.whyItMatters: Related operations can share a name, making the interface natural while still supporting different input types or parameter counts.
understand.explain: Overloads should have consistent meaning. Avoid ambiguous conversions and confusing combinations of defaults. Test overloads with literals and typed variables so you understand which signature is selected.

examples.title: Overload by type
examples.code: int area(int side){return side*side;}\ndouble area(double radius){return 3.14*radius*radius;}
examples.explanation: Different parameter types select different signatures; this naming example is pedagogical and represents two area interpretations.

examples.title: Overload by count
examples.code: void log(const std::string& text);\nvoid log(const std::string& text,int level);
examples.explanation: The parameter count distinguishes the functions.

examples.title: Call selects type
examples.code: void show(int);void show(const std::string&);\n// show(42) selects the int overload
examples.explanation: The argument type selects a viable function.

examples.title: Return type cannot distinguish
examples.code: // Invalid overload pair: int f(int); double f(int);
examples.explanation: Identical parameter lists cannot be overloaded only by return type.

examples.title: Distinct calls
examples.code: void draw(int);void draw(double);\n// draw(2) selects int; draw(2.5) selects double
examples.explanation: The argument types provide clear overload selection.

practise.guidedTask: For Function Overloading Basics, analyze each example and record the parameter signature, call, chosen behavior, state changes and result. Identify any compile-time constraints or design caveats.
practise.independentTask: Create a focused C++ exercise on Function Overloading Basics. Include several cases demonstrating the main concept, plus tests for typical, boundary and invalid/ambiguous cases as appropriate. State the expected behavior and verify each case.
hints: Identify the concept being demonstrated before tracing code.
Use small, explicit examples to verify behavior.
Compare at least two contrasting cases.
Check compiler rules, lifetime and error paths relevant to this topic.
Keep the code focused and explain the observed output/result.
